summary: A seat that restarts without a fresh session keeps its held work leases under the new incarnation

replay.detail: No forced replay. work.rebound transfers only an exact held lease and replays idempotently. Orphaned or released leases are never resurrected. A possibly resumable session retains its existing lease until a binding or fresh intent resolves continuity, or ordinary lease expiry releases it.

schema.detail: Registers the work.rebound claim kind (fields, system-only write policy, durable retention) in the claim registry, so the registry digest changes. No table, index, trigger or schema-version change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or rules-digest changes. A fleet capability barrier gates the new ownership protocol.

compatibility.detail: Emission of work.rebound and resumable-session orphan deferral require every current fleet member to advertise work_rebind_v1>=1. Ambiguous membership, missing support or unfenced outside writers close the barrier. While closed, ownership keeps the prior orphan/reclaim behavior. Older members retain unknown facts; no new transfers are emitted during a mixed-version roll.

downtime.detail: Normal rolling binary restarts. Session transfers activate only after the fleet capability barrier opens.

manual.detail: No operator cutover. Capability advertisements automatically open or close the writer barrier; native-session publication, proof and transfer commit atomically.

recovery.detail: A rollback stops advertising work_rebind_v1 and closes the barrier, so no further transfers are emitted. Already retained work.rebound facts remain authoritative on supporting readers; older readers retain but do not apply them.
